step_by_step_solution: Standard form: x + y + s1 = 4; x + s2 = 2; y + s3 = 3. The slack variables s1, s2, s3 form the initial basis (all decision variables = 0).

Tableau 0 (initial): basic solution s1 = 4, s2 = 2, s3 = 3; Z = 0. Cj - Zj values: x: 3, y: 5. y has the largest positive Cj - Zj (5), so y enters the basis. Minimum-ratio test (RHS / pivot-column entry, positive entries only): s1: 4/1 = 4; s2: - (entry 0 is not positive); s3: 3/1 = 3. The minimum ratio is in the row of s3, so s3 leaves. Pivot element = 1 (row 3, column y). Row operations: R3(new) = R3 (pivot is already 1); R1(new) = R1 - R3(new); R2(new) = R2 (entry in the pivot column is already 0).

Tableau 1: basic solution s1 = 1, s2 = 2, y = 3; Z = 15. Cj - Zj values: x: 3, s3: -5. x has the largest positive Cj - Zj (3), so x enters the basis. Minimum-ratio test (RHS / pivot-column entry, positive entries only): s1: 1/1 = 1; s2: 2/1 = 2; y: - (entry 0 is not positive). The minimum ratio is in the row of s1, so s1 leaves. Pivot element = 1 (row 1, column x). Row operations: R1(new) = R1 (pivot is already 1); R2(new) = R2 - R1(new); R3(new) = R3 (entry in the pivot column is already 0).
Tableau 2: basic solution x = 1, s2 = 1, y = 3; Z = 18. All Cj - Zj <= 0, so the current solution is optimal (maximisation rule).
Optimal solution: x = 1, y = 3; maximum Z = 18.
